_comment: THE HAND REVIEW OF THE 2023-POPULATION TEST. Written by a person, from the documents
the two machine passes put on disk. Neither of those files is ever edited by hand and
neither carries a verdict: scope.md, 'A machine classification never writes to the
record' -- it writes to a file whose name says it is machine output, with every verdict
null, and a person moves what survives review. This is that person's file.
ONE ENTRY PER IEA REFERENCE, and every field is a reading of a named document.
owner_or_permit_pre_cutoff   IS THERE A DOCUMENT BY THE OWNER, A PERMIT AUTHORITY OR A
REGULATOR, DATED AT OR BEFORE 31 OCTOBER 2023, THAT NAMES
THIS PROJECT. An owner's newsroom index that never names
the project is a record of looking, not a document about
the entry, and it does not make this true (D-C3).
site_named / capacity_as_stated / fid_stated / start_as_stated / input_stated
what the document SAYS, quoted or closely paraphrased,
for rungs 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6. Empty means the documents read
do not say it -- which is a fail, not a silence.
<rung>_source / _speaker / _date / _precision
the document the cell cites, who was speaking in it, and
its date at the precision the document itself carries.
announced_start              the owner's stated start as of the cut-off where there is
one; the builder falls back to the vintage's own year and
records which it used.
outcome and its fields       one of the six frozen values, as of 30 September 2026,
with the speaker, the source and the date that carry it.
note                         anything a reader of the table would need and the columns
cannot hold.

entries.note: Three documents are on file from at or before the cut-off and none is about this project. The IEA's own reference is a conference slide deck hosted by the Estonian Hydrogen Association, which answered with an empty body; h2est.ee's front page and newsroom are that association's, not an owner's. EDP is a partner in GreenH2Atlantic at Sines and its own front page (2017) and newsroom (2023-06-20) are on file, and NEITHER NAMES THE PROJECT -- the apparent 'sines' hits are the word inside 'businesses'. So the entry is reported and not scored.

entries.site_named: a mega-hydrogen facility in Eemshaven, province of Groningen; 'Green hydrogen production, initially in the Eemshaven'
entries.capacity_as_stated: green hydrogen production expected to be around 800,000 tonnes per year by 2040
entries.note: Gasunie's own release of 27 February 2020, with Groningen Seaports and Shell Nederland. THE LIST'S MEGAWATTS ARE THE OWNER'S WIND FARM: the owner states '3 to 4 gigawatts' of WIND generation in 2030 and 800,000 tonnes a year of hydrogen by 2040, and the vintage carries 4000 MWel. So the capacity on file is in tonnes and is recorded in tonnes; no conversion is made and the two figures are not the same quantity. FID: 'The project starts with a feasibility study' -- no decision on file. Start: '3 to 4 gigawatts in 2030' is a wind figure and 'by 2040' is a capacity date, so no operation start with a precision this register can record. The OCI letter of intent is dated 31 March 2022 but was read live, with no capture at or before the cut-off, and 'letter of intent' is firmness intent in any case.

TWO OWNER DOCUMENTS, BOTH ABOUT THE PILOT AND NOT ABOUT THIS ENTRY. HYBRIT Development's own article (captured 2021-02-12) and Vattenfall's release of 3 October 2019 name Luleå, Malmberget and Svartöberget -- all of them the PILOT plant and the hydrogen store beside it. This entry is HYBRIT DEMO, and the only thing either document says about it is that the partners 'are already looking into the possibility of scaling up the manufacturing by building a demonstration plant in 2025'. That is a possibility, not a site, not a capacity, not an FID, and not an operation start. The Innovation Fund list the IEA also cites answered with an empty body. The entry is a DRI perimeter exclusion as well, and the clause travels with it.

Carbon Recycling International is the owner and nothing of CRI's is on file. The IEA's reference is a CRI slide deck hosted by CO2 Value Europe, which answered with an empty body; the two other documents are CO2 Value Europe's own front page and newsroom, and that is an industry association. Reported, not scored.
The October 2023 vintage carries no http reference for this entry, so there was nothing of the publisher's own to read and no host to ask the archive about. Reported, not scored.

entries.site_named: the Fertiberia plants of Puertollano (Ciudad Real) and Palos de la Frontera (Huelva)
entries.note: Iberdrola's own release, dated on the page 'PR (2020-10-28)'. IT IS ONE SENTENCE ABOUT FOUR PROJECTS AND IT IS NOT A CAPACITY FOR THIS ONE: '800 MW of green hydrogen production capacity' is the Iberdrola-Fertiberia PARTNERSHIP, and 'plans to develop three additional projects between 2023 and 2027' is the programme this entry is one of. No megawatts and no start date are stated for Puertollano II, and passing rung 2 on the programme figure would let one sentence carry the rung for four entries. FID: 'could see the installation' -- no decision. The vintage's 2027 is plainly read off 'between 2023 and 2027', which is a development window and not an operation start.
No http reference in the vintage. Reported, not scored.

entries.site_named: Site location in Maade industrial area close to the port of Esbjerg; footprint of app. 30 ha
entries.capacity_as_stated: the 1GW plant; electrolysis technology on gigawatt level
entries.note: The owner's own project site, Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners' HOEST PtX Esbjerg, captured 2023-09-01 with no dateline of its own, so the date is the capture as an upper bound. FID FAILS ON ITS OWN WORDS: 'Final investment decision due in 2025', which is rung 3's 'planned for' exactly. START FAILS ON A RANGE: 'Expected to enter full operation in 2028/29' names two years and this register's vocabulary records one, so reading it at year precision would mean choosing a year the owner did not choose. That is the 'mid-decade' case arriving in a new shape and it is asked of the questions file rather than settled here. The site's news page also records a grid connection agreement signed with Energinet on 05.01.2023 and an offtake agreement with Monjasa; the offtake is not an input, and rung 6 for this entry is scored from the dependency graph because the entry is an admitted row.

entries.note: ITM Power's own news page, no dateline on the page, so the date is the capture as an upper bound. Immingham is a town and the speaker is the owner, so rung 1 passes at municipality level under the rung's own words. FID FAILS AND THE DOCUMENT SAYS WHY IN AS MANY WORDS: 'the pathway to a final investment decision' and 'the main goal is to now reach a final investment decision in the next 18-months'. The Sheffield gigafactory in the same page is ITM's own factory, not this project's site, and it was not read as one.

Three references, none of them with a capture at or before the cut-off: the Financial Times refused, and Greentech Media and Fuel Cells Works were read live in 2026. A live page read in 2026 cannot date anything to 2023. Reported, not scored.

entries.capacity_as_stated: scaling up the production capacity of the electrolyzers from 100MW in 2025 to 1,85GW in 2035
entries.start_as_stated: 100MW in 2025 -- and, further down the same page, 'HyNL will be increasing production capacity from 100MW in 2026 to 1.85 GW in 2035'
entries.note: ENGIE's own HyNetherlands project site. THE PAGE GIVES TWO START YEARS FOR THE SAME 100 MW STEP -- 2025 in one paragraph and 2026 in another, with '140 kilo tons per year of CO2 starting from 2026' beside it. One speaker, one document, two years: that is not a slip, which is a speaker changing its mind over time, and it is not a disagreement between speakers either. Both are recorded and neither is chosen. Rung 5 passes because a start with year precision IS on file; which year it is remains open. 'Province of Groningen' on its own would have failed rung 1 as coarser than a municipality; the Eems power plant at Eemshaven is what passes it.

entries.site_named: 'The ENGIE hydrogen production site will be located on the site of the Eems power plant in Eemshaven, 30 kilometers north-east of the city of Groningen'

The roadmap runs from 100 MW in 2025 (or 2026) to 1.85 GW in 2035 and names NO 900 MW step, so the vintage's 900 MWel for a second phase has no owner figure behind it on file and rung 2 fails. The site passes on the same sentence as 595: the production site is one site and the owner names it.

bp is the owner and NOTHING OF BP'S ABOUT THIS PROJECT IS ON FILE FROM BEFORE THE CUT-OFF. Two bp releases were read -- 18 December 2024 and 23 July 2026 -- and both are live 2026 reads with no capture at or before 31 October 2023, so neither is evidence about the cut-off. bp.com's front page has a capture dated 2023-10-31 and does not name the project; the only newsroom path the index holds under bp.com at or before the cut-off is a 438-character page captured in 2001. The Wall Street Journal capture of 2023-06-07 is a newspaper. Reported, not scored.

THE CONTRACTOR SPEAKS AND THE OWNER DOES NOT, which is the one case rung 1 was written to exclude. Worley's own pages -- a release captured 2023-08-02 and its newsroom captured 2023-10-10 -- carry Holland Hydrogen, and Worley is the engineering contractor, not the owner: Shell is, and www.shell.nl answered with nothing and has no capture at or before the cut-off. H2 View is a trade title and the Innovation Fund page the authors cite refused. So there is no owner, permit or regulator document from before the cut-off, and rungs 1, 2, 3 and 5 are not searched as of it. Rungs 4 and 6 are still scored, because the funder pass and the dependency graph are population-wide files with their own dates and the brief reads them for every entry.

entries.site_named: the Fertiberia plants of Puertollano (Ciudad Real) and Palos de la Frontera (Huelva)
entries.note: ONE DOCUMENT ANSWERS FOR FOUR ENTRIES AND THE LINE SAYS WHICH DOCUMENT. The reference the vintage gives for this entry is an Iberdrola page that answered with nothing, and the Iberdrola release of 28 October 2020 that IS on file -- fetched under refs 508 and 783 -- names Palos de la Frontera (Huelva) among the Fertiberia plants the partnership's projects are to be built at. Failing rung 1 here for want of a document this register demonstrably holds would be scoring its own filing convention as the owner's silence (D-C4). The only other pre-cut-off document is Sevilla ABC, a newspaper. No capacity and no start is stated for this entry, for the same reason as at ref 508: the 800 MW and the 2023-2027 window are the programme's.

entries.site_named: 'The electrolyser of at least 200 MW will be located in the Port-Jerome industrial zone' -- the project's own site, and the French page adds the commune of Saint-Jean-de-Folleville

entries.fid_stated: 'Air Liquide announces an investment of over 400 million euros for the construction of its Normand'Hy electrolyzer, with a capacity of 200 MW'
entries.start_as_stated: 'La mise en service est prevue pour 2025'
entries.note: THE RICHEST PRE-CUT-OFF FILE IN THE POPULATION SO FAR: Air Liquide's own project site, its French newsroom and its group newsroom, all captured before the cut-off. Rung 3 passes on the owner ANNOUNCING the investment rather than planning it -- 'announces an investment of over 400 million euros for the construction' -- and the register itself reads the same sentence the same way: the row airliquide-normandhy-port-jerome moves announced to fid on 14 September 2023 on exactly this statement, so the rung and the row agree without either having been adjusted to the other. Rung 5 passes on 'la mise en service est prevue pour 2025': rung 5 admits a year and, unlike rung 3, has no clause against an expectation. The prefecture's authorisation to operate (19 January 2022) is a permit fact the owner reports and it would have carried rung 1 on its own.

REVISED AFTER READING REF 821, AND THE REVISION IS THE POINT OF D-C4. Read on its own, this entry had no owner document: the reference the vintage gives it is the H2V NORMANDY consultation file, which is another of the owner's projects 300 km away, and the register holds that one as ref 807. The Dunkirk project's OWN documents were fetched under ref 821, H2V 59's second phase -- h2v59-concertation.net captured 2023-09-23, which names the commune of Loon-Plage, and h2v.net captured 2023-10-27, which gives 'Premiere phase: 2 unites de production de 100 MW (= 200 MW)', the exact figure the vintage carries for this entry. Both are the owner speaking before the cut-off about this plant. An entry reviewed in isolation would have been reported as unsearched while the register held the answer under the next reference number. FID: the page says the first phase 'a obtenu en novembre 2022 tous les permis prefectoraux necessaires a sa mise en exploitation', which is a permit and not an investment decision; the 2019 infographic's '230 a 251 million d'euros investis' is an infographic and does not say the decision was taken. START FAILS ON A RANGE: the infographic gives 'Mise en service entre 2022 et 2023', two years, and this register's vocabulary records one -- the same shape as ref 532's '2028/29'.

Three rungs pass and the list's two numbers both have an owner's sentence behind them. FID fails on the owner's own words -- 'les etudes sont en cours pour la deuxieme phase'. THE PUBLISHER'S REFERENCE FOR A 100 MW ELECTROLYSER IS A RELEASE ABOUT A BIOFUELS PLANT. Repsol's own release of 23 October 2020, captured 2023-10-03, announces 'Spain's first advanced biofuels plant in Cartagena' -- 250,000 tonnes a year of hydrobiodiesel, biojet, bionaphtha and biopropane for EUR 188 million -- and the only hydrogen in it is that the facility 'will include the commissioning of a hydrogen plant that will fuel a new hydrotreatment unit'. That is a hydrogen unit for a hydrotreater, with no capacity, no technology and no electrolysis. Repsol's release about its 'first large-scale renewable hydrogen plant in Cartagena' exists and was read, but live in 2026, with no capture at or before the cut-off. So there is no owner document about THIS entry from before the cut-off.

Both references are topsectorenergie.nl, a Dutch programme organisation and not the owner, and both answered with under 400 characters -- a refusal under the empty-body rule. Nothing readable at or before the cut-off.

The vintage's only reference is klimaatakkoord.nl, the Dutch Climate Accord's own site, which is neither the owner nor a permit authority, and which answered with 345 characters. Its front page carries 1,261. Reported, not scored.
The same klimaatakkoord.nl reference as refs 845 and 847, and the same answer. Reported, not scored.
The same klimaatakkoord.nl reference as refs 845 and 846. Reported, not scored.

NEL IS THE ELECTROLYSER SUPPLIER AND EVERFUEL IS THE OWNER. Two of the three references are Nel's -- one answered with nothing, and nelhydrogen.com's front page was captured 2023-10-19 and does not name this project. Bioenergy International answered with nothing and Fuel Cells Works with 234 characters. A supplier's page is not the owner's, and rung 6 would not read it either: it asks for the OWNER naming the supplier.

Smartenergy is the owner and its page has no capture at or before the cut-off -- it was read live in 2026. What is on file from before the cut-off is Cinco Dias, a newspaper, captured 2022-12-01. Reported, not scored. Smartenergy's own domain was also on the press list when this entry was fetched, which cost it a newsroom leg; the list was corrected and the entry re-fetched.

The authors' quality-check reference is a Hydrogen Europe page, which answered with 307 characters, and Balkan Green Energy News answered with nothing. Hydrogen Europe is a trade association and its front page and newsroom, both captured before the cut-off, do not name White Dragon. H2 View is a trade title and was read live. Reported, not scored.

The consortium's own site, captured 2023-09-23, names the project throughout its news page -- the Joint Development Agreement of 21 October 2020, IPCEI status on 18 November 2021, and NOT being selected by the ETS Innovation Fund on 26 November 2021. So somebody who is party to the project spoke before the cut-off and rungs 1, 2, 3 and 5 are fails rather than silences. WHAT IT NEVER SAYS IS WHERE: the nearest thing to a location is 'reduce CO2 emissions in North Sea Port', and North Sea Port is a cross-border port authority spanning Ghent and Terneuzen -- coarser than a municipality and in two countries. No capacity, no FID and no operation start are stated for the full-scale phase. The Joint Development Agreement is an agreement among the partners and not an input supply, so it does not reach rung 6.

STEAG's own reference answered with nothing and its front page with 101 characters -- both refusals under the empty-body rule -- and IJGlobal was read live. Nothing readable at or before the cut-off. The entry is also a DRI perimeter exclusion and the clause travels with it.
El Periodico de la Energia, a trade title, was read live; El Economista's URL would not resolve at all. Nothing readable at or before the cut-off.

entries.site_named: 'an electrolysis plant with a capacity of more than 100 MW is to be built at the site of the RWE power plant in Lingen'
entries.capacity_as_stated: an electrolysis plant with a capacity of more than 100 MW
entries.note: The GET H2 initiative's own project page for GET H2 Nukleus -- bp, Evonik, Nowega, OGE and RWE Generation -- captured 2023-05-21 with no dateline, so the date is the capture as an upper bound. RWE's own reference and one of its row sources answered with nothing before the cut-off, and rwe.com's front page and press index, both captured before it, name Lingen only in a project menu. THE PHASE IS NOT IN THE DOCUMENT: the page describes one plant of 'more than 100 MW' at the RWE Lingen site and says nothing about a second phase, which is the same file the drift ruling of 17 September 2026 found the publisher re-describing between vintages. Rung 5 fails on what the page does say: 'By 2024, the GET H2 partners want to jointly establish the first publicly accessible hydrogen infrastructure' is a target for the 130-kilometre NETWORK from Lingen to Gelsenkirchen, not a production start for this electrolyser.

entries.site_named: 'a mega-hydrogen facility in Eemshaven'; 'Green hydrogen production, initially in the Eemshaven and later possibly also offshore'
entries.note: The same Gasunie release of 27 February 2020 as ref 5, which is the only document on file for either phase. For the SECOND phase it says 'the ambition to grow to about 10 gigawatts around 2040' -- and that is wind generation, not an electrolyser, so the vintage's 6000 MWel has no owner figure behind it. 'Around 2040' is also not an operation start: it is when the wind capacity is to have grown.
One document from before the cut-off, S&P Global Commodity Insights, captured 2023-08-02. A trade title is not the owner, and Grupa Lotos's own pages are not on file at all.

entries.site_named: 'Hamburg Moorburg'; 'Auf dem Grundstueck des ehemaligen Heizkraftwerk[s] ... im Herzen des Hamburger Hafens'
entries.capacity_as_stated: an electrolyser 'of 100 megawatts', with the site's further development into a 'Green Energy Hub' planned around it
entries.start_as_stated: 'Wenn alle Genehmigungen und Freigaben rechtzeitig erteilt werden, kann die Wasserstoffproduktion 2026 starten'; 'wird hier ab 2026 jede Menge sauberer Wasserstoff produziert'
entries.note: The project's own site, hghh.eu, captured 2023-09-23, and its news page captured 2023-01-30 carrying the release of 28 May 2021 in which Shell, Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Vattenfall and the municipal Waerme Hamburg are named as the partners. Moorburg is a district of Hamburg and the decommissioned power-station site is named, so rung 1 passes comfortably. RUNG 5 PASSES ON A CONDITIONAL YEAR AND THAT IS DELIBERATE: rung 3 is the rung with the clause against 'expected' and 'subject to', and rung 5 is not -- it asks for a start with a precision this register can record, and 2026 is one. The link to Vattenfall's Dan Tysk and Sandbank wind farms is a grid connection, not a contracted input.

entries.site_named: 'The most advanced project to date is in As Pontes (A Coruna) and will have a 100 MW electrolyser and six associated wind farms'
entries.capacity_as_stated: a 100 MW electrolyser (As Pontes), with six associated wind farms of 611 MW combined
entries.note: Endesa's own release of 1 February 2021, captured 2023-09-22 in English and, at ref 910, in Spanish. THIS IS THE ONE PROJECT IN THE 23 THAT THE OWNER GIVES ITS OWN NUMBERS: 'a 100 MW electrolyser', 738.2 million euros, a production of 10,000 tonnes of green hydrogen, 18 months to build. FID fails because the document is a LETTER OF INTEREST to the Ministry for the Ecological Transition -- 'Endesa has presented the Ministry with a letter of interest to develop up to 23 projects' -- which is the opposite of a decision taken. No operation start year is stated: what the release gives are durations, 18 and 24 months, with nothing to count them from. The six wind farms are Endesa's own generation and not a contracted input.

entries.site_named: 'Los proyectos peninsulares de electrolizacion (As Pontes, Huelva, Teruel, Almeria, Tarragona, Valle del Ebro, Compostilla y Sesena)'
entries.note: The Spanish original of the Endesa release read at ref 906, captured 2023-09-22 and dated on the page '01 febrero 2021'. Huelva is named as one of the eight peninsular electrolysis projects, which carries rung 1 at municipality level. THE CAPACITY IS AGGREGATE AND IS NOT THIS ENTRY'S: '8 electrolizadores con una capacidad de 315 MW' for the eight together, and 340 MW across all 23. As Pontes is the only one the release sizes on its own, so the vintage's 100 MWel for Huelva has no owner sentence behind it. Same letter of interest, so no FID; no start year for Huelva.

One readable document from before the cut-off, Renewables Now, captured 2023-04-01. The consortium's own file on static1.squarespace.com answered with 324 characters, which is a refusal under the empty-body rule, and Fuel Cells Works with 385.

entries.site_named: 'large-scale production of green hydrogen at the Maasvlakte area in Rotterdam'; 'a hydrogen plant on the site of Uniper'
entries.capacity_as_stated: a capacity of 100MW, to expand this capacity to 500MW
entries.start_as_stated: 'the ambition to realise a hydrogen plant on the site of Uniper by 2025' (8 February 2021), restated as 'commission 100 MW of Plug electrolysis capacity to produce green hydrogen by 2026' (7 March 2023)
entries.note: TWO OWNER DOCUMENTS TWO YEARS APART, AND THE SLIP IS ON FILE BEFORE THE CUT-OFF: Uniper said by 2025 on 8 February 2021 and by 2026 on 7 March 2023. One speaker changing its mind, which is what the slip rule is for, and the later date is what rung 5 rests on. FID FAILS ON THE OWNER'S OWN CONDITION: 'Plug will deliver 10 prefabricated PEM electrolyzer arrays for Uniper's flagship project, H2Maasvlakte UPON UNIPER'S POSITIVE FID'. Rung 6 for this entry is scored from the dependency graph rather than from this review, because the entry is an admitted row -- and the Plug selection is an equipment order, which is the kind that graph carries most of.

entries.site_named: 'large-scale production of green hydrogen at the Maasvlakte area in Rotterdam'
entries.start_as_stated: 'rapidly expanding that capacity to 500 MW by 2030 at the latest'
entries.note: The same two Uniper releases as ref 927. The owner states a TOTAL of 500 MW by 2030; the vintage's 400 MWel for the second phase is 500 minus the first phase's 100, which is the IEA's arithmetic and not a sentence anybody published, so rung 2 fails. Rung 5 passes on 'to 500 MW by 2030 at the latest', which is a date for this phase's capacity being in service and carries a year.

entries.site_named: 'The planned large-scale pilot plant will be deployed nearby Castellon (Spain), in one of the most important ceramic industrial clusters in Europe'
entries.capacity_as_stated: 'German cleantech company Sunfire supplies a 100 MW pressurized alkaline electrolyser'
entries.start_as_stated: 'With sufficient funding in place, the operational start of the electrolyzer is planned by early 2024'
entries.note: Smartenergy's own page, dated 'Valencia/Wollerau/Dresden/Roma, 04 Febuary 2021'. RUNG 1 PASSES ON A HEDGE AND THE HEDGE IS RECORDED: 'deployed nearby Castellon' names the town, with the owner speaking, which the rung admits at municipality level -- but 'nearby' is the owner declining to say which municipality, and whether that should pass is asked of the questions file rather than settled here. Rung 5 passes on 'by early 2024' at year precision. Rung 6 fails although a supplier is named: 'in the scope of the project, Sunfire supplies a 100 MW pressurized alkaline electrolyser' states no order and no contract, and firmness is what rung 6 turns on.

Recharge and Barron's both refused, and the one readable pre-cut-off document is windfair.net, a wind-industry news site, captured 2022-06-25. H2 Green Steel's own pages are not on file. The entry is also a DRI perimeter exclusion.
The single reference is H2 View, a trade title, and its URL would not resolve. Nothing readable at or before the cut-off.
The single reference is an investor-relations page on ir.q4europe.com, which answered with nothing. Nothing readable at or before the cut-off.

entries.site_named: 'Our facility in the Port of Amsterdam'; 'Its location at the Port of Amsterdam allows it to take advantage of an existing kerosene pipeline to Schiphol airport'
entries.start_as_stated: 'The factory, which is scheduled for completion in 2027, will produce 50,000 tonnes of SAF annually'
entries.note: SkyNRG's own page for Synkero, captured 2023-10-03. RUNG 2 FAILS ON A UNIT THAT IS NOT THIS PLANT'S ELECTROLYSER: the only figure is '50,000 tonnes of SAF annually', which is the product of the synfuels plant, and the vintage's 100 MWel is an electrolyser rating. Converting one into the other is what the three-units rule forbids, and recording the SAF tonnage as the electrolyser's capacity would be the same error by another route.
